newsitem.title: USA: New Brunswick Pwr still sees nuke plant up in Nov.
newsitem.headline: New Brunswick Pwr still sees nuke plant up in Nov.

text.p: New Brunswick Power Corp still expects its 630 megawatt (MW) Point Lepreau nuclear power plant to return to service in November after being shut in late September to repair boiler tube leaks, the company said.
"The station will be shut down until early November," a company spokesman said on Wednesday, adding crews continued to inspect for leaks in all four of the reactor's boilers.
Technicians have been checking boilers' instrumentation and replacing eroded pipes inside the boilers, he said.
To make up for loss of Point Lepreau, the utility has increased generation from its hydro and fossil-fueled plants, and bought spot power supplies from Hydro-Quebec, he said.
The utility estimated replacement energy costs at C$350,000 a day on top of the several million dollars for repairs.
The Lepreau nuclear station is 45 kilometers south of the city of St John.
Based in Fredericton, New Brunswick Power has a total installed capacity of 4,000 MW.
